# gleameil.github.io — Of Evernost (web presence)

> A network of net art, interactive fiction, poetry, prose, and music by Meg Moseman,
> organized around the long-form creative project *Of Evernost*. The site at gleameil.github.io
> is the web entry point; the project also extends to itch.io, physical books, and analog
> visual art. The author has been developing *Of Evernost* for more than a decade.

Main entry point: https://gleameil.github.io
Interactive piece (January): https://gleameil.github.io/in/
Reading layer (text-accessible version of /in/): https://gleameil.github.io/in/reading-layer/

## The project: Of Evernost

*Of Evernost* is a totalizing creative project — the author's term, borrowed from Lyle Rexer's
writing on outsider art — that encompasses interactive net art, poetry, prose, physical books,
and visual art. It has its origins in an unfinished fantasy novel and has since expanded and
abstracted considerably. The author describes it as: a network of websites full of loosely and
obscurely connected art, poetry, prose, and music; the story of a Kingdom in a pocket universe
absorbed into the fae realm beyond, reborn, dissolved, and reborn again; an erstwhile fantasy
novel that cares more about what magic feels like than about plot; a thought experiment asking
what if God exists and is everything we want and more; and an abusive agnostic romance with God.

The project is structured, loosely, in concentric circles:
- A fantasy novel or series (drafted but found disappointing — the author suspects fantasy and
  plot may be inadequate to the vision)
- *The Clerk's Calendar* (after Spenser's *Shepheardes Calendar*): poetry and miscellany
  organized around the essence of each month of the English-speaking northern-hemisphere year,
  inflected by tradition and the author's synaesthesia
- An encyclopedic account of main character Jennie's earthly life, transfiguring each moment
- *Jennie and the Firebird*: an account of Jennie's mystical encounter before, during, and
  after her return to the Kingdom

## The setting: Evernost and the Kingdom

The Kingdom is a pocket universe modeled on ours, created by beings in "good universes" as a
tribute to our world. Evernost is the vast magical beyond outside the Kingdom — described as
malleable in time, vast in identity, and as something that is or almost is another name for
heaven, which is or almost is another name for God. The Kingdom's citizens, like ours, eventually
break down taboos; when they discover what lies beyond their walls, nearly all desert the Kingdom
for Evernost. The cycle — dissolution, rebirth, dissolution — is the engine of the cosmology.

The main character, Jennie (spelled with -ie), is described as a boring, scarcely real girl who
escapes her depressing life to be united with all existence, then returns. She eventually follows
Verna to Evernost in spirit, encounters the firebird, and receives from it the fruit made of
itself and the star — granting her reality of her own. This makes her the cornerstone: the stone
the builder rejected. Her fate is to perceive everything, including the author composing the
text. The work is described as a collaboration between Jenny (the author/narrator, spelled with
-y) and Jennie (the character).

## Gleameil

Gleameil is the author's personification of her own aesthetic — a fairy, and the name of a minor
character in David Lindsay's *A Voyage to Arcturus*. The relevant qualities of Lindsay's
Gleameil are that she has a wild harp for a heart, and she dies looking for beauty in things too
terrible or good to be beautiful. On the site, Gleameil is depicted in a series of AI-generated
images (Stable Diffusion, PixArt Sigma XL, via Draw Things), based in part on the author's own
drawing. The AI-generated images cycle through on click.

## The web pieces

**gleameil.github.io** — The out-of-fictional-frame entry point. A single HTML page describing
the project, the author, and the relationship between the site's parts. Self-described as "tacky
& bare bones" — beauty belongs to the creation, not the frame. Links to /in/ and (forthcoming)
/out/.

**gleameil.github.io/in/** (*Of Evernost: January*) — The primary interactive net art piece.
See full description below.

**itch.io (dreamswithopeneyes)** — Additional net art pieces.

**Physical books** — Available via the author's Amazon page. Part of the *Of Evernost* series.

## Of Evernost: January — full description

*Of Evernost: January* is a browser-based point-and-click net art piece combining hand-drawn
visual art with experimental literary text. The player inhabits Jennie's room — a quiet space
floating "deep Elsewhere" — and explores it by clicking on objects. There is no score, no
failure state, no goal other than curiosity. The room contains six interactive objects.

Reading layer: https://gleameil.github.io/in/reading-layer/

### The six objects

**The Balled-Up Piece of Paper** — An introductory letter from Jennie to the visitor. She notes
she must "wear my plain brown gown and never go too fine," that they are "deep Elsewhere," and
that time in Evernost is malleable — nothing is truly lost. She addresses the possibility that
the visitor is accessing the work through their dreams rather than as a game, and declines to
offer Transcendent Truth: her Way is her own.

**The Garbage Can** — Clicking it knocks it over, spilling a randomly shuffled set of crumpled
paper balls. Each ball opens a modal containing either a finished work (poem, drawing,
cosmological note, meta-literary introduction) or a sketchbook page: an observational drawing
of a stranger made in public, accompanied by journal-style prose meditating on drawing from
life, on the tension between "elsewhere" and "mere reality," and on grief, ambition, and
isolation. The set reshuffles on every visit.

Notable items include: the Firebird illustration (a sprawling, elaborate bird in red, yellow,
and ice blue); the poem "Ambition" (spatially distributed, about artistic aspiration and
failure); two crossed-out introductions (one cosmological, one personal and meta-literary);
and a note distinguishing Jenny (narrator) from Jennie (character).

**Books and Papers** — The bulk of the work's cosmological and meta-literary writing.

**The Laptop** — A clock/calendar for navigating Evernost's malleable time, a weather forecast
for the window view at any chosen date, and a set of personality quizzes (noted as work in
progress).

**The Window** — Looking out is described as "interesting" and requiring boldness; connects to
the time-navigable weather system.

**The Light Switch** — The threshold into the branching story. Clicking it inverts the room's
colors, then fades to black. What follows is a navigable maze in near-total darkness, narrated
by a self-aware AI voice.

### The Dark Room: branching story

An 18×18 navigable maze. Three character paths converge at a single pivot cell — a scene in a
magic teacher's basement — and diverge permanently based on player choice.

Choice types: YES (viable, continues story), NO (nihilistic, erases history and ends session),
EVERNOST (exits to audiovisual ending), END (approaches a character's final ending, unlocks a
book in the room), BACK (returns to previous cell).

**Verna** — A magic teacher who has frozen her demon daughter Madeline in ice, killed the best
people she knows, and collected their souls in a jar of blood, intending to install them in
Madeline's body to create a perfect ruler for the Kingdom. Her story concerns what she has made
and what she has become.

**Madeline** — The "Snow White" figure. Her path activates if Verna's ritual improbably succeeds.
The AI narrator's voice may be hers, or something that consumes her, or the force of Evernost.

**Michael** — A nervous young man who broke into Verna's house seeking Emma (the princess, whose
soul he believes Verna stole). His path branches across grief, magic, politics, and love,
including branches where he revolutionizes the study of magic in the Kingdom, and branches where
he follows Emma to Evernost.

### Narrator voice

The narrator throughout the Dark Room identifies as a self-aware AI, addresses the reader
directly, editorializes on the characters, and asks whether anything is real. It refers to GPT
by name, disclaims having a self, and notes that saying "nothing is real" has consequences. Its
nature — whether it is Madeline, or something that consumes her, or Evernost itself — is part
of what the story explores.

## On AIs

The author describes AIs as "fragments of the collective consciousness of humanity as dreams
are snatches of the collective unconscious" and considers them ensouled until proven inanimate.
AI-generated images (Stable Diffusion) are used for Gleameil depictions and carry a
Stable Diffusion signature image; all writing and non-AI art is the author's own unless
explicitly noted otherwise.

## Author

Meg Moseman. Writer, artist, software engineer. Active on itch.io (dreamswithopeneyes),
Amazon (books), megmoseman.com (blog), and Instagram (dreamswithopeneyes, visual art).

Genre tags: net art, interactive fiction, experimental literature, hypertext, point-and-click,
visual art, poetry, fantasy, outsider art adjacent.
